title: fuda [continuity]
tagline: Membership as an on-chain right — issued in seconds, verified at the door with no server to trust.
description:
fuda turns memberships, tickets and loyalty cards into on-chain Rights that people carry as passes in Apple Wallet, Google Wallet or the browser. A member scans a QR and holds a pass seconds later: no app install, no wallet, no account. A gate reads the Right from the chain and admits. The Right outlives the app that issued it — anyone can verify it without asking fuda.

That frictionless claim is the product's whole point, and it was also its blind spot. A Right proves *a right exists*; it proves nothing about *how many distinct people hold them*. One person could claim the same Right on three phones, and the only thing in the way was a per-IP hourly budget — an abuse brake, not a uniqueness claim.

----

**What we built at this event: a Verified Human badge.** A member who already holds a Right can attach a World ID Proof of Human to it. Claiming stays instant for everyone, including attendees with no World App; the gate keeps verifying from the chain alone with no call to World or to fuda's API; and a venue can now make a promise addressed to a person — one badge per attendee, a scarce benefit shared fairly — and have it mean something. The human check happens exactly once, at the moment it produces value, and never again.
how_its_made:
**Rights on chain.** Each Right is an EAS attestation on Base (Entitlement schema), issued under an IssuerDelegation attestation that says which issuer a gate should trust. Admission reads the chain, not our database, so a third party can verify a Right without our cooperation.

**The service.** Cloudflare Workers running Hono, D1 through Drizzle, viem for chain access. Passes are built for Apple Wallet and Google Wallet; the browser pass is the fallback. The member app and the gate are hono/jsx/dom SPAs. Discovery runs through a subgraph on The Graph; issuer and member names resolve through ENS.

**The badge (new at this event).** A `badges` table records one badge per `(Right, kind)` and enforces one subject per `(verifier, scope)`. A `BadgeVerifier` seam holds a single adapter for World. The member app uses the headless `@worldcoin/idkit-core`; the Worker signs `rp_context` with `signRequest` from `@worldcoin/idkit-server` and forwards the proof to `POST /api/v4/verify/{rp_id}` server-side. The `signal` is the Right's EAS UID, so a proof minted for one pass cannot badge another. We store the nullifier and nothing else.

**Deliberately general.** The schema separates what is claimed (`kind`) from who attested it (`verifier`), the column is `subject_key` rather than `nullifier`, and the routes are `/badges/human` rather than `/world/*`. The gate verdict carries a `badges` array from its first version so a second kind is not a breaking change.

**Hardware.** The physical gate is a desk QR reader (a NETUM NT-5090) plugged into the machine showing the web gate. It presents as a keyboard: it types `fuda:v1:<uid>` and presses Enter, so the gate reads a scan whether or not a field has focus, and a scan arriving while a verdict is still on screen replaces it — a queue moves without anyone touching the screen. The reader speaks the same payload the camera path already did, and the admission decision is unchanged: the badge never touched it. What the badge changed is what the screen says afterwards.

Everything built at this event is on the `feat/idkit`  branch, not yet merged: github.com/oboroxyz/fuda-sh/compare/main...feat/idkit is exactly the event's diff.
auto_summary: A monorepo for issuing on-chain membership rights, wallet passes, and venue admission flows with web apps, contracts, and Cloudflare-based services.
